current_route.title: Optimization of Low-High Index Two-Layer AR Coating
current_route.scientific_hypothesis: A two-layer stack with the low-index material (SiO2) adjacent to air and the high-index material (TiO2) adjacent to the glass substrate will achieve a lower arithmetic mean reflectance across the 450-700 nm band than the reverse ordering, given the thickness constraints of 40-160 nm.
current_route.design_principle: Impedance matching theory suggests that stepping the refractive index from air (1.0) to substrate (1.52) via an intermediate low index (1.46) then high index (2.40) creates a smoother effective index gradient than starting with a high index jump, potentially reducing Fresnel reflections over a wider spectral range.
current_route.proposed_topology: Air / SiO2 (variable thickness) / TiO2 (variable thickness) / Glass (n=1.52)
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (450-700 nm)
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thicknesses must remain within 40 nm to 160 nm
Exactly one layer of each material
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave and non-quarter-wave optimization principles for broadband AR
expected_advantages: The Low-High ordering provides a better match to the substrate index profile, likely yielding lower average reflectance compared to High-Low ordering which may suffer from strong front-surface reflection.
known_risks: The optimal thicknesses for this specific ordering might fall outside the 40-160 nm constraint window, forcing a sub-optimal solution at the boundaries.
The constant-index assumption may not perfectly match real dispersion, though the problem mandates constant indices.
current_route.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar stack: Incident Medium Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 SiO2 (Gao) (lossless, n=1.46), Layer 2 TiO2 (Siefke) (lossless, n=2.40), Substrate Glass (lossless, n=1.52). Optimize the thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2 simultaneously. Constraints: Thickness of each layer must be between 40 nm and 160 nm. Objective: Minimize the arithmetic mean of power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees) sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm in 5 nm steps. Use seed 17. Allow maximum 64 solver evaluations. Report the best found thickness pair, the resulting reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance.
